setup: Sit on an upright bench or stand tall
Narrow grip on the inner bends
Press the bar overhead to straight arms
execution: Bend your elbows to lower it behind your head
Keep your upper arms close to your head
Go to a deep stretch you can control
faults: Don't let your elbows flare wide

notes: Use light to moderate weight and warm up; the deep stretch loads the elbows.
Seated with back support makes it easier to keep the lower back from arching.
Get the bar overhead and back down to your lap or the floor in a controlled way, ideally from a seated start.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at head height, figure seated on an upright bench facing right. The bar dropping behind the head while the upper arms stay up must be clear.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Seated tall, back on the pad, feet flat. EZ bar held overhead on the inner grips, arms straight, upper arms beside the ears.

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Elbows bent well past 90°, bar lowered behind the head toward the upper back. Upper arms still close to the head and pointing up; ribs down.

guideBrief.barPath: An arc from overhead down behind the head and back
emphasise: Upper arms stay by the head
Deep, controlled stretch behind the head
Lower back stays on the pad

sources.title: Maeo et al. 2023, Eur J Sport Sci 23(7): Triceps hypertrophy greater after overhead vs neutral-arm elbow extension training
sources.supports: Why the overhead position is worth an entry: 21 adults, 12 weeks of cable extensions; the overhead arm grew more in every triceps head despite lighter loads.
sources.note: Abstract only, read through Europe PMC. Cable extensions, mostly untrained participants; not this exact exercise.
